A human frontend engineer has one advantage over the most advanced AI coder possible.
They are human. And software is designed for humans to use.
A human coder can test as they go and build from their perspective as user with stresses, a like, and hands made of flesh.
They will be slower at the coding but at validating innovation.
An AI coder will build existing concepts infinitely faster.
But A.I. Innovation will be slow.
A.I.'s will need to rely on human-based user-research practices to build confidence in novel approaches.
Their infinite efficiency will grind to a halt when it comes to innovation.
Ironically, the human advantage will be in their ability to ignore common human centred design practices at times.
(low level ones that they should already ignore)
Then again, not all software is for human interaction, and even less may be in the future.
And A.I.'s strong point is predicting things we often can see or articulate.
How unpredictable will our day to day thoughts and feelings remain the more superpowered and interconnected AI becomes?
